summary: Two verified Reuters stories cover Saudi-reported missile/drone interceptions and a US diesel-price decline. The FAA follow-up is held for missing public predecessors. This is a partial metadata edition; the complete styled companion remains unpublished.
limitations: Targeted Reuters coverage only. Earlier uncovered intervals remain open and no verified fully completed source-scan cutoff is established.

Reuters original publication dates are verified as 15 November 2026. Exact initial-publication versus later article-update times cannot be distinguished and remain unknown. Displayed headers are not treated as event times.
The Saudi account attributes interceptions to the coalition; no new oil-production loss or attributable oil, FX or bond-price reaction is established.

The US diesel observation is from Saturday, 14 November, before this edition's four-hour window. It is labelled catch-up, despite appearing as new in the producer's report. It is a historical retail price, not a live quote, released CPI result or Fed decision.
FAA story R-20261113-US-FAA-NATIONAL-GROUND-STOP version 6 is held because public predecessor versions 1–5 are absent. The story has not been renamed or reset to version 1.
The producer could not access other briefing automations, so cross-report checking is limited to retained accessible history. This does not imply exhaustive Reuters coverage.

Metadata previews only. The complete source narrative and presentation review copy are retained privately. Full styled hourly publication is held because the approved publisher lacks an hourly channel, time-aware edition identity and exact-edition full-report reader links.

sources.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts missiles towards Riyadh, drones in Eastern Province
US diesel below $6 a gallon at 2-month low on easing tensions, weaker demand

stories.headline: Saudi-led coalition reports intercepting two missiles and three drones
stories.body: Reuters reported the coalition's account of two Houthi ballistic missiles intercepted towards Riyadh and three drones over the oil-rich Eastern Province. The report describes earlier attacks on Aramco facilities. It does not establish a new production interruption from these interceptions. The exact attack time and any attributable oil, currency or bond-market movement remain unverified.
stories.analysis: Energy-infrastructure security warrants attention. An interception announcement does not establish damaged facilities, lost output or a confirmed export disruption.
stories.watch_next: Saudi Energy Ministry and Aramco statements, independently verified damage, production continuity and shipping conditions.

stories.headline: US average diesel falls below $6 per gallon; observation predates this window
stories.body: Reuters attributed a Saturday, 14 November, US average retail diesel price of $5.998 per US gallon to GasBuddy, below $6 for the first time in two months. The reported record was $6.519 on September 22. Seasonal demand weakness, recovering refinery activity and lower crude prices helped the decline; Brent futures had fallen 18.5% over the preceding two weeks. These are historical observations, not live quotations. No attributable contemporaneous Treasury-yield or dollar movement was verified.
stories.analysis: If sustained, lower diesel costs could ease freight and farming expenses. This does not establish a CPI decline, a consensus surprise or a Fed rate decision.
stories.watch_next: Wholesale fuel and freight prices, duration of the decline, and subsequent CPI/PCE releases.
